 New recruits shine as Roar overcome Glory in Brisbane
 ALEAGUES.COM.AU WRITERS
 23 October, 2026

 Brisbane Roar have opened their A-League Men campaign with a 2-1 win over Perth Glory at Suncorp Stadium, with goals from Justin Vidic and star recruit Nam Tae-hee.
 A wonder strike by South Korea international Nam Tae-hee has lit up Suncorp Stadium in Brisbane Roar’s 2-1 win over Perth Glory.

 View this post on Instagram 
 High-profile signing Nam, playing his first A-League Men match for the club, struck in the 42nd minute with a goal of pure class on Friday night to get the Roar’s campaign off to a winning start. 
 The attacking midfielder tipped a bouncing ball up for himself just outside the box and then let rip with a right-foot rocket into the roof of the net.
 CLICK HERE TO GET YOUR TICKETS TO THE 2026/27 A-LEAGUE MEN SEASON 
 Striker Justin Vidic opened the scoring for the Roar in the 28th minute. 
 The Glory hit back on the hour mark when substitute Matthew Ellis scored with his first touch in the ALM after being on the field for just 33 seconds.
 Ellis’s strike came after a shocking back pass by Roar defender Joel King, who was playing his first game for the club after a move from Sydney FC.
 Stefan Colakovski should have equalised but sprayed his shot with an open goal in front of him.
 The Roar fielded seven new players in their starting side and most of them provided impetus.
 Full back Tate Russell set up the opening goal after working hard to intercept  goalkeeper Matthew Sutton’s throw out and then delivering a pinpoint cross for Vidic to steer home.
 The Roar, after finishing a disappointing 11th last season, started well with the midfield in control. 
 The deadly left foot of Tyrese Francois has received rave reviews from coach Michael Valkanis in the pre-season. Defender Tom Aldred set him up beautifully but the former Fulham midfielder shot just wide from outside the box.
 Vidic, who was everywhere, headed just over the bar not long after scoring as winger Sabit Ngor, formerly with Central Coast, created plenty of chances.
 Pieter Jacobsz had the Glory’s best chance in the first half when he had an open goal to hit but sprayed his left-foot shot wide.
 Striker Tom Lawrence also fired wide just after the break as Perth failed to capitalise on chances.
 Roar goalkeeper George Plusnin, in his first ALM match, was composed but was not put under enough pressure by the visitors.
 The Roar welcomed back former stalwart skipper Aldred to the side after two seasons in India and he excdelled in the captain’s armband.
